question: to the Commission João Oliveira (The Left) Subject:

The goal of the ‘Global Sumud Maghreb’ international humanitarian land convoy is to deliver urgent humanitarian aid to Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, who are being denied access to basic goods required for survival as a result of Israel’s criminal blockade. On 24 May 2026, ten activists from this international humanitarian convoy were stopped and detained in Sirte, in eastern Libya, while negotiating safe passage through a security checkpoint. The 10 activists, including a Portuguese citizen, have been incommunicado ever since and their whereabouts are unknown. In view of the above: 1.

What steps does the Commission intend to take to establish the whereabouts of the Portuguese citizen and ensure her rights and those of the other members of the international humanitarian convoy are respected?
Will it intervene to help secure the release of the Portuguese citizen and the other activists of the humanitarian convoy and request their free passage to Gaza?

What diplomatic steps is it taking to bring an end to Israel’s criminal blockade against Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, put a stop to Israel’s violations of international law and establish the State of Palestine, as UN resolutions have been advocating for decades?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (7.8.2026) Member States authorities are responsible for consular protection and the security of their citizens. The EU can confirm that the ten activists from the international humanitarian convoy, including the Portuguese national who had been detained in Sirte, Libya, since 24 May 2026, have been released. The Commission welcomes this outcome and the fact that they were able to return safely. The humanitarian situation in Gaza is of grave concern, and the EU has been constantly calling on Israel to allow immediate, unimpeded access and sustained distribution of humanitarian assistance at scale into and throughout Gaza as well as to reopen border crossings and comply with international humanitarian law, thereby upholding its obligations under international law. Since 2023, the EU provided over EUR 674 million in humanitarian assistance for Palestine1, working with trusted and certified partners to ensure aid reaches those most in need. The EU understands the goal of the flotilla’s participants to deliver much-needed aid to people in desperate need. At the same time, the EU discourages such initiatives due to the risks to participants’ safety and potential for escalation, and because the best way to deliver humanitarian assistance to Gaza is to do it through established channels. The EU is firmly committed to a lasting and sustainable peace based on the two-state solution. The EU is ready to contribute to all efforts towards this solution and call on all parties to refrain from actions that undermine its viability. The EU will equally continue to work with regional and international partners, including through the Global Alliance.
1 This designation shall not be construed as recognition of a State of Palestine and is without prejudice to the
individual positions of the Member States on this issue.
